paper_metadata.title: Creep behavior of polycrystalline and single crystal Ni-based superalloys coated with Ta-containing NiCoCrAlY by high-velocity oxy-fuel spraying

evidence.quote: Polycrystalline and single crystal Ni-based superalloys coated with Ta-containing NiCoCrAlY by high-velocity oxy-fuel spraying were creep tested at 980 °C under 150 MPa constant load in air
Commercial Ta-containing NiCoCrAlY powder (Amdry 997, Oerlikon Metco) was utilized to deposit thermally-sprayed coatings (BC) on two different Ni-based superalloys (SA).

attributes.description: reduction of superalloy section thickness degrades creep life

evidence.quote: fewer grains across the specimen thickness decreases the creep resistance
creep damage in metals is essentially the nucleation, growth, and coalescence of intergranular microcracks up to specimen rupture
the M247LC-SX fracture occurred primarily by void growth and linkage ( Fig. 4 b)
the oxygen diffusion causes grain boundary embrittlement in IN100 and void growth and linkage in M247LC-SX
in both cases, the oxygen diffuses into the alloy forming a region of internal oxidation of aluminum
giving a Norton exponent ( n ) of 9.5 and 7.3 for IN100 and M247LC-SX superalloys, respectively
